Delhi-NCR woke to a cooler, rain-soaked Friday after overnight showers pulled temperatures below normal. The IMD has forecast more rain and thunderstorms, while heavy to very heavy downpours are expected across parts of eastern and central India, with flash-flood risks flagged in vulnerable areas. Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR) saw a cool Friday morning after overnight rain swept across the city, lowering temperatures and bringing a noticeable chill to the air, signalling the early onset of winter. The sudden spell of showers on Thursday prompted a noticeable drop in temperatures across the region, setting the stage for the winter chill to settle over Delhi-NCR. On Thursday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a yellow alert for Delhi and its adjoining NCR, forecasting spells of rain and thunderstorms over the region in the next 24 to 48 hours, followed by clear weather heading into early November. According to the Regional Meteorological Centre in New Delhi, widespread weather activity is likely across Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurugram and Faridabad. The forecast also predicts generally cloudy skies with one or two spells of light to moderate rainfall, along with thunderstorms and lightning across several parts of the city. It also expects isolated pockets of the region to experience heavy rain during the night. The rain is likely to continue on Friday, with light showers forecast in several areas and isolated moderate rain possible from morning to forenoon. The maximum temperature for Friday is likely to be between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is expected to be between 16 and 18 degrees Celsius. The weather agency expects minor traffic disruptions on roads today and warns of an increased chance of vehicle accidents and water accumulation in low-lying areas and on roads. It also suggests checking for traffic congestion on your route before leaving for your destination. Follow any traffic advisories issued in this regard. Avoid going to areas that are often prone to waterlogging. Delhi-NCR weather on Thursday Dark clouds hung over Delhi since morning, and the city recorded trace rainfall in the last 24 hours. The maximum temperature at Safdarjung, Delhi's base weather station, settled at 25.4 degrees Celsius, 5.6 degrees below normal. It was the lowest October high since October 8, 2022, when the maximum temperature was 23.4 degrees Celsius. Maximum temperatures ranged from 20.6 degrees Celsius in Haryana's Karnal to 27.4 degrees Celsius in Punjab's Patiala, with Delhi's base weather station, Safdarjung, recording 25.4 degrees Celsius, about 5.6 degrees below normal. Heavy rain forecast across eastern and central states; flash flood risk flagged Meanwhile, states in central and eastern India face intense precipitation due to the remnant cyclonic circulation, along with isolated extremely heavy rainfall forecast over north Bihar on Friday and parts of Chhattisgarh and Odisha. Additionally, widespread heavy to very heavy downpours are also expected in Jharkhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and East Uttar Pradesh. Overnight rain brought a noticeable drop in temperatures across Delhi-NCR, signalling an early winter chill. The city's AQI improved to 133, while the IMD issued a yellow alert forecasting more rain and thunderstorms over the next 24–48 hours.
October 30, 2026 / 05:46 IST
Overnight rain brings a drop in Delhi temperatures and improves AQI to 133
Overnight rain brought a noticeable change in weather across Delhi-NCR, with a drop in temperatures and a nip in the air signalling the onset of cooler conditions.
Late-night visuals from areas around Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station and Jamia Millia Islamia showed rain-soaked roads and steady showers as dark clouds covered the city.
The spell of rain also coincided with an improvement in Delhi's air quality. The city's Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 133 in the Moderate category at 4 am on Friday, down from readings above 200 in the Poor category on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a yellow alert for Delhi and adjoining National Capital Region (NCR) districts on October 29, forecasting rain and thunderstorms over the next 24 to 48 hours. Clearer weather is expected to return in early November.
Delhi-NCR weather forecast: More rain, thunderstorms expected
According to the Regional Meteorological Centre in New Delhi, widespread weather activity is expected across Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurugram and Faridabad.
The forecast indicates generally cloudy skies, with one or two spells of light to moderate rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning across several areas. Isolated locations could receive heavy rain during the night.
The wet spell is expected to continue into October 30, with very light to light rain forecast across multiple locations and moderate showers during the morning and forenoon.
The IMD expects skies to turn partly cloudy on October 31, with no weather warnings in place. Conditions are forecast to become mainly clear on November 1 and 2, with green-coded alerts indicating fair weather across the districts.
Heavy rain alert for Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and other states
Meanwhile, central and eastern parts of the country are likely to see intense rainfall due to a remnant cyclonic circulation.
The IMD has forecast isolated extremely heavy rainfall in north Bihar on October 30 and parts of Chhattisgarh and Odisha. Heavy to very heavy rain is also expected across Jharkhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and East Uttar Pradesh.
A low-to-moderate flash flood risk has been flagged until October 30 across vulnerable watersheds in several districts. These include Korba, Surguja and Balrampur in Chhattisgarh; Sundargarh, Keonjhar and Sambalpur in Odisha; Palamu and Simdega in Jharkhand; East and West Champaran, Rohtas and Bhojpur in Bihar; and Sonbhadra, Ghazipur and Ballia in East Uttar Pradesh.
South India to see increased rainfall from November 2
The IMD has also forecast an increase in rainfall activity across southern peninsular India from early November as a Bay of Bengal weather system approaches.
Scattered showers are expected to continue through the end of October. Fairly widespread to widespread rainfall is forecast over Coastal Karnataka, Kerala, South Interior Karnataka, Telangana and Coastal Andhra Pradesh between November 2 and 4.
Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam are likely to receive isolated very heavy rainfall on November 2 and 3. Telangana is also expected to experience thundersqualls, with strong gusty winds reaching speeds of up to 60 kmph.
